title: D-VSync: Decoupled Rendering and Displaying for Smartphone Graphics
problem: The VSync-based rendering architecture on smartphones tightly couples the rendering pipeline to the display refresh cycle, causing frame drops and increased rendering latency when large high-frame-rate screens and complex visual effects (physics-based animations, stunning UI) demand rendering time that exceeds the VSync interval. This rigid coupling prevents flexible scheduling of rendering work across display periods.
motivation: Modern smartphones are adopting high-frame-rate screens (90-144 Hz) with increasingly complex visual effects, placing unprecedented pressure on the traditional synchronized rendering-display architecture that was designed for simpler, lower-frequency displays.
method: D-VSync decouples the rendering pipeline from the display refresh cycle by separating the rendering scheduler from the VSync signal, allowing rendering to be completed asynchronously relative to display timing. The system introduces a buffering and synchronization layer that permits rendering jobs to run beyond a single VSync period and uses predictive scheduling to align rendered frames with the nearest available display window, reducing the frequency of missed frames.
key_novelty: Decoupling rendering from VSync by allowing asynchronous rendering completion with predictive display-cycle-aware frame scheduling, eliminating the hard coupling that forces frame drops when rendering overshoots the display interval.
contributions: D-VSync architecture decoupling rendering scheduler from VSync display cycle
Asynchronous rendering completion with buffering layer for frame alignment
Reduction in frame drops and rendering latency on high-frame-rate smartphone displays
Implementation and evaluation on Android/OpenHarmony rendering stacks

metrics.other: reduced frame drops and rendering latency (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: VSync-coupled rendering (Android, OpenHarmony, iOS standard rendering service)
